title: Lung-bearing vertebrates descend from an ancestor with a swimbladder

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Lung-bearing vertebrates descend from an ancestor with a swimbladder

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: All vertebrates with true lungs have descended from an ancient ancestor that had a swimbladder used for flotation, which natural selection converted into a lung.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I can, indeed, hardly doubt that all vertebrate animals having true lungs have descended by ordinary generation from an ancient prototype, of which we know nothing, furnished with a floating apparatus or swimbladder.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Means of transition.”. Scope: vertebrates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-09: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern phylogenomic, developmental, and anatomical data directly address homology and transition direction. The ancient organ's precise flotation function remains less securely recoverable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Combine vertebrate phylogenies with developmental, anatomical, and gene-expression characters for lungs and gas bladders, and reconstruct the ancestral organ and its function. Homology and an ancestral flotation bladder support the claim; independent origins or an ancestral lung refute its stated direction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Deep ancestral-state direction can remain model-sensitive.

Functional use in the ancient ancestor is inferred indirectly.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public trees and morphological matrices make the direction of the transformation a standard ancestral-state problem, and that direction is the core of the historical claim. Soft-tissue function at the critical nodes is inferred rather than observed, so the flotation premise and the appeal to selection stay out of reach of the same datasets. The analysis is feasible for living osteichthyans and only a proxy for the unknown prototype.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Code lung versus swim bladder, and flotation versus respiration, on a molecular vertebrate tree and reconstruct the ancestral state for lung-bearing vertebrates. The claim is supported if that ancestor is reconstructed as having a flotation swim bladder and lungs are derived from it; it is refuted if lungs (or a non-flotation air organ) are ancestral and swim bladders arise later inside ray-finned fishes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The flotation function and soft anatomy of the deep ancestor are rarely fossilized.

Selection as the converting agent is not recorded by character order alone.

Coding lung and swim bladder as alternative states can smuggle in a homology decision.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.58
data existence: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.52
